name: ffmpeg-skill
cost: Free and open source (MIT), no API keys or account
works_with: Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, Gemini CLI and any MCP client
short: Gives your coding agent 42 local FFmpeg tools to cut, caption, reframe and export video, then check the result.
what: ffmpeg-skill is an agent skill that teaches your agent a fixed routine: probe the file, edit it, then check and verify the output. It ships 42 tools that run `ffmpeg` and `ffprobe` on your machine for cuts, joins, silence removal, captions, overlays, loudness, platform exports and more. Every tool can also be called as an MCP tool.
who: People who edit video with a coding agent and want the work to stay on their own machine. If you only need a one-off trim, plain FFmpeg will do.
needs: FFmpeg 6.1 or newer with the components it needs (on a Mac the README says to use `ffmpeg-full`)
Node 16 or newer, only for the `npx` installer
Optional: a local speech engine such as faster-whisper, only for captions from speech

steps.title: Install FFmpeg
steps.text: This is the Ubuntu and Debian command. On a Mac the README uses `brew install ffmpeg-full`, and on Windows `winget install Gyan.FFmpeg`.

steps.title: Install the skill
steps.text: This installs it for Claude Code. Add `--cursor`, `--codex` or `--all` for other agents.

steps.title: Check your machine
steps.text: It lists which FFmpeg components are present and which tools can run.

steps.title: Or install it as a Claude Code plugin
steps.text: This works in Claude Code 2.1.275 or later and needs no Node.

steps.title: Or run it as an MCP server
steps.text: For clients that have no shell.

try.label: From the README
try.text: Take `interview.mp4`, keep 0:45-3:10 and 5:00-6:30, and make it exactly 60 seconds for Reels.

watch: The tools write files. With the `overwrite` option they replace an existing file, so keep a copy of your original footage.
A plain Homebrew `ffmpeg` on a Mac lacks some filters, so a few tools will not run until you install `ffmpeg-full`.
The optional speech engines download their model weights the first time they run. The audio itself stays on your machine.
Installed copies do not update by themselves. Run `npx ffmpeg-skill` again to refresh.
